Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates bilateral widening of the lower posterior mediastinum with lateral displacement of both paraspinal lines (indicated by arrowheads) and smooth margins, without vertebral destruction or respiratory symptoms. This radiographic appearance is characteristic of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma involving the posterior mediastinum, distinguishing it from neurogenic tumors (typically unilateral) or extramedullary hematopoiesis (associated with anemia/blood disorders not mentioned).
